---
title: "How suggestions work"
description: "Shared mechanics of the bot suggestion workflows: when they run, what they review, and how their suggestions reach you."
---

Three workflows propose changes to your package instead of just checking
it: [author suggestions](authors-suggest.qmd) for `DESCRIPTION`,
[roxygen suggestions](roxygen-suggest.qmd) and
[test suggestions](test-suggest.qmd). They share how
their changes reach you. What happens inside the roxygen and test
workflows, step by step, is shown [under the hood](suggestions-internals.qmd).

## When they run and what they review {#what-gets-reviewed}

The workflows run on pull requests and, if your caller adds a `push`
trigger, on pushes to your working branches. The roxygen and test
workflows can also run on a schedule or by hand. Every run reviews **only
what is new since the last review**:

| Event | Reviewed |
|---|---|
| A pull request is opened or reopened | everything the PR changes |
| Another push to an open PR | only the commits of that push |
| A push to a branch without a PR | only the commits of that push |
| The first push of a new branch | the commits that exist on no other branch |
| A schedule or manual run | what changed on the branch since its last review, see [scheduled and manual runs](#scheduled-runs) |

How far your branch is ahead of or behind `dev` doesn't matter. Some
commits are left out, because they aren't new work on your branch or were
already reviewed:

- **commits merged in from another branch**, e.g. when you merge `dev`
  into your branch to catch up: they aren't reviewed, and their authors
  aren't credited on your branch;
- **the bot's own commits**, e.g. after you merge its suggestion PR: it
  doesn't review its own suggestions again;
- **commits a pull request run already reviewed**, e.g. a feature merged
  into `dev`: a later scheduled run on `dev` doesn't review them again.

A `paths` filter in your caller decides whether a run starts at all, e.g.
only when files under `R/` changed. The examples on each page show the
triggers.

## Suggestions are pull requests, never direct commits

A bot never commits to your branch. When a workflow has something to
suggest, it

1. commits each changed file separately on a branch
   `bot-suggest/<kind>/<your branch>`;
2. opens a pull request from there **into your branch**;
3. on a PR, comments on it, e.g.

   > **Roxygen documentation suggestions** opened: #19 (into `feat/my-feature`)
   >
   > 2 changes applied · 1 not applied
   >
   > - `R/ds.wrapper.R`

   The other titles are "Test suggestions" and "Update contributors in
   DESCRIPTION".

You review the suggestion like any PR: merge it, edit it first, or close
it. In roxygen and test suggestion PRs, every suggestion that changes a
file is a **checkbox** in the description: untick what you don't want, or
tick a suggestion that wasn't applied, and the branch follows — see
[choosing suggestions](suggestion-choices.qmd).

### One suggestion PR per branch

While a suggestion PR is open, further runs **add to it** instead of
opening another one:

- your new commits are merged into the bot's branch, and where both
  changed the same lines, **your version wins**;
- the new suggestions are added on top;
- if you changed a file that already has a suggestion, it is reviewed
  again against your current code, and the new suggestion replaces the
  old one.

So you can push and keep working before you look at the suggestions.

**The description is one report.** For roxygen and tests it is rebuilt
on every run from all findings so far: each finding is tagged with the
commit it came from, findings that no longer hold are crossed out with
the reason (never deleted), and a "Latest review" line says what the last
run changed. Edits you make to the description by hand are overwritten —
except the checkboxes, which are read first. Comments on the PR are
safe. The author suggestions add a section per run instead.

The description also records, invisibly, up to which commit the bot has
reviewed. That's how a run that was dropped or failed in between is
caught up.

The bot's branch is **rebuilt** instead (with a note in the PR) when your
branch's history was rewritten, e.g. by a rebase and force-push, or when
your new commits can't be merged into it automatically. Then it contains
only that run's suggestions. If you'd rather always have only the latest
run's suggestions, set the input `open-suggestion-pr: replace`.

::: {.callout-note}
## One gap, by design
GitHub keeps at most one waiting run per branch. If you push three times
within a few minutes while **no** suggestion PR is open, the middle push's
run can be dropped, and its files are only reviewed when they change
again or in a [full review](#full-review). Nothing wrong is proposed; one
review is missing.
:::

### When a Claude call fails

The roxygen and test workflows retry a Claude call that fails for a
passing reason (rate limit, overloaded, a lost connection). If it still
fails, the run goes on with the other files and stays green; the file is
named in a **warning** on the run's summary page and in the pull
request's checks. While a suggestion PR is open, the next run checks that
file again, even if nothing changed in it.

## Scheduled and manual runs {#scheduled-runs}

The roxygen and test workflows can also run on a schedule (e.g. monthly)
or by hand ("Run workflow"). They review **what changed on the branch
since its last review**, so nothing is reviewed twice:

- **A scheduled run** reviews `dev`, since GitHub always starts a schedule
  on the default branch (usually `main`).
- **A manual run** reviews the branch you choose in the menu.
- **The `review-branch` input** sets a fixed branch for both, e.g.
  `review-branch: main` in a repository without `dev`.

The last review is read from the workflow's earlier runs, so the caller
grants `actions: read` and `checks: read` (the examples do). Before a
branch has been reviewed at all, a scheduled or manual run has nothing to
compare with: it reviews nothing and becomes the starting point — run a
full review once instead. The suggestions go into a suggestion PR into
that branch, as for a push.

GitHub stops scheduled workflows in repositories without activity for 60
days. Add the [workflow keepalive](workflow-keepalive.qmd) so the
scheduled runs keep running.

## Full review {#full-review}

With `review-scope: all`, the roxygen and test workflows review **every**
`R/*.R` file of the branch, whatever changed, and collect everything in
one pull request into that branch, from
`bot-suggest/<kind>-all-<branch>-YYYY-MM`, titled "Roxygen documentation:
full review" or "Test suggestions: full review". Running a full review
again in the same month updates that month's pull request.

The example callers offer it as a choice in "Run workflow": a `scope`
input passed on as `review-scope`. A full review on every schedule is
possible too, but costs a Claude call for every function each time.

## What gets proposed {#what-gets-proposed}

A suggestion should be a real improvement, not a reworded sentence or an
extra test for its own sake. So Claude has to state a **reason** for every
change, from a fixed list, and only some reasons lead to a proposal:

| Workflow | Proposed | Dropped |
|---|---|---|
| Roxygen | `missing`, `inaccurate`, `incomplete` | `clarity`, `style` |
| Tests | `uncovered_branch`, `error_handling`, `edge_case`, `regression` | `other` |

On top of that, the workflows drop documentation changes that differ only
in whitespace, punctuation or case, and tests whose assertions already
exist. A suggestion you declined (unticked) isn't proposed again while
the function's code stays the same.

The reasons, what each means, and which are proposed are set in
`config/suggestion-policy.yml`, together with the other rules: at most 10
new tests per function, which possible bugs in the code are reported and
which get an issue, and [where reports go](#where-reports-go). Change it
[per repository](#adjusting-the-guidance), or per caller with two inputs
of the roxygen and test workflows:

- **`accept-reasons`**, e.g. `missing,inaccurate,incomplete,clarity`;
- **`code-issue-confidence`**: which possible bugs are reported, by how
  sure Claude is (`high`, `high,medium`, `high,medium,low`), or `none`
  for no such reports at all.

These settings are a first guess, likely to be tuned.

The test workflow also changes **existing tests**, but only for fixed
reasons: an update when the function's behaviour was changed on purpose
(`contract_changed`), a deletion for a duplicate, removed behaviour or a
trivial test. A test that fails because the code may be wrong is only
reported. See [existing tests](test-suggest-review.qmd#existing-tests).

### Where reports go {#where-reports-go}

Findings that don't change a file — possible bugs in the code, failing
tests, names that may already be listed — go into the suggestion PR's
description. Without a suggestion PR, they go where `routing` in
`config/suggestion-policy.yml` says:

| Report | On a pull request | Without a pull request |
|---|---|---|
| Roxygen: possible bugs in the code | a comment | one issue per month |
| Tests: the report | a comment | an issue |
| Tests: each failed generated test | a comment | in the report |
| Authors: may already be listed | a comment | the job log |

Each can be set to `comment`, `issue` or `log`; an issue needs
`issues: write` on the caller (the roxygen and test examples grant it).
A comment isn't posted again on the next push if it says the same.

## Housekeeping

- **The bot never reviews itself:** runs on a `bot-suggest/*` branch are
  skipped, for pull requests and pushes alike.
- **Some runs do nothing, with a notice in the log:**
  - branch deletions and tag pushes;
  - pull requests from forks and from Dependabot, which get no secrets;
  - draft pull requests, until they are marked ready (add
    `ready_for_review` to the caller's `pull_request` types).
- **Runs of the same branch take turns:** a push run and a PR run for one
  branch never write the suggestion branch at the same time.
- **Cleanup:** [Cleanup suggestion branch](cleanup-suggestion-branch.qmd)
  deletes a `bot-suggest/*` branch once its pull request is merged or
  closed.
- **Checks on suggestion PRs:** with the
  [GitHub App](getting-started.qmd#github-app) configured, your required
  checks run on suggestion PRs; without it they don't, and a ruleset
  requiring them would block the merge.
- **Generated code gets no tokens:** the test workflow runs the tests it
  writes in a separate R process without the Claude and GitHub tokens.

## Where a suggestion comes from {#provenance}

Each report ends with a small line naming the model, short fingerprints of
the prompts and settings as used, and the workflow version, e.g.
"Made with claude-sonnet-5-5 · prompts 3f2a… · config 91c0… ·
datashield-workflows a1b2c3d". The same is stored, hidden, in the
description. So a suggestion can later be traced to what made it, also
after the prompts changed.

When a suggestion PR is closed, the
[suggestion choices](suggestion-choices.qmd#outcome) workflow adds a
hidden record of what happened to each suggestion. Nothing leaves the
repository.

## Adjusting the guidance {#adjusting-the-guidance}

The workflows read their settings, guidance and prompts from this
repository. To change one for your package only, put a file at the **same
path** in your repository. Settings files are **merged over the shared
ones key by key**: yours only needs the entries you change, and later
additions to the shared file still reach you. A list is replaced as a
whole.

| File | Controls |
|---|---|
| `config/suggestion-policy.yml` | Reasons and which are proposed, the number of new tests, possible bugs, author roles and name particles, where reports go |
| `config/claude.yml` | Claude model and request settings, per task |
| `config/bot-authors.yml` | Accounts never added to `DESCRIPTION` (bots, and coding assistants such as Claude Code), and how the bot recognises its own commits |
| `config/report-style.yml` | Heading levels and spacing of the suggestion reports |
| `config/roxygen-style.yml` | Roxygen tag order and per-tag guidance |
| `config/datashield-role-guidance.yml` | Roxygen guidance for DataSHIELD client, server and utility packages |
| `config/datashield-example-env.yml` | The demo-server login used in DataSHIELD client examples |
| `config/test-categories.yml` | Meanings of test file categories (`test-<category>-<R file>.R`), see [test files](test-suggest.qmd#test-files) |
| `config/test-role-guidance.yml` | Testing strategy given to Claude |
| `config/dslite-canned-datasets.yml` | The DSLite datasets a new DataSHIELD test setup can use |
| `config/workflow-outcomes.yml` | What workflows produce, for the [workflow graphs](workflow-graphs.qmd) |
| `prompts/*.md` | The full prompts sent to Claude |

For example, to also propose clearer wording in roxygen documentation,
your `config/suggestion-policy.yml` needs only:

```yaml
roxygen:
  reasons:
    clarity:
      accept: true
```

A prompt is the one exception: your copy **replaces** the shared one, so
start from a copy of it. The settings of the
[analysis scripts](datashield-analysis-details.qmd#settings) work the same
way.

::: {.callout-note}
## Before v1: JSON, and replaced as a whole
Until v1, some of these files were JSON (`bot-authors.json`,
`roxygen-style.json`, `test-categories.json`, `test-role-guidance.json`),
replaced the shared file completely, and `config/claude.yml` held
`accept_reasons`. A copy with the old name is no longer read: move what
you changed into the new YAML file, keeping only your entries.
:::
